evidence_quote: 1 Date: 1/22/26 This weekly report from the New York State Department of Health presents summaries of select ongoing and emerging infectious disease outbreaks of interest to public health professionals and the public, both globally and in the United States. The Global Health Update summaries include preliminary and up-to-date data that are publicly available for these events at the time of posting. Because this report aggregates and summarizes data and information from outside sources, the quality, accuracy or completeness of that data, and the appropriateness of the methodology used, cannot be guaranteed. Please refer directly to those sources for any data questions. Because the report includes preliminary information, subsequent reports may contain updates or revisions to information in prior reports. .......................................................................................................... 17 Chikungunya United States – Second Locally Acquired Case of 2025 Reported in Florida: According to data the Florida Department of Health (Florida Health), a locally acquired case of chikungunya was reported during the week ending January 17, 2026. The case was reported in Miami-Dade County and experienced symptom onset in December 2025. This is the only locally acquired case reported in Florida during 2025. Florida last reported local transmission of chikungunya in 2014. A total of 328 travel associated were reported during 2025, primarily among individuals with recent travel history to Cuba (316). In October 2025, the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH) reported the ﬁrst conﬁrmed locally acquired case of chikungunya ever in the state among an individual from Nassau County. According to data from the United States CDC, these are the ﬁrst locally acquired cases to be reported in the United States since 2015. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), a resurgence of chikungunya was observed in several regions globally during 2025, particularly in the Americas, with signiﬁcant potential for further spread and new introductions in previously unaﬀected areas. Source: Florida Health (1/26) 2 Diphtheria Nigeria – Resurgence Observed in 2022 Continues Through 2025: According to data from the Nigeria Center for Disease Control (NCDC), as of December 28, there have been a total of 20,032 suspected cases of diphtheria, of which 15,273 are conﬁrmed, and 872 deaths among conﬁrmed cases reported in Nigeria during 2025. Case and death totals for 2025 are higher and more geographically dispersed compared to 2024. Source: NCDC Marburg Ethiopia – No Incident Cases Reported for 40 Consecutive Days: According to the Africa CDC, as of January 22, 2026, there have been 14 conﬁrmed Marburg cases and 9 deaths reported in Ethiopia since the outbreak was ﬁrst declared on November 14, 2025. No incident cases or deaths were reported since the previous update. There have been 5 recoveries and there are no contacts currently under follow up. A total of 40 days have passed without any incident cases reported – 42 days must pass for the outbreak to be declared over. Cases have been reported in Jinka town and Hawassa city, both locations in southern Ethiopia. Since the outbreak began, over 3,800 individuals have been tested for infection. This is the ﬁrst Marburg outbreak in Ethiopia – previous outbreaks and sporadic cases have been reported in other African counties, including Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Ghana, Kenya, Equatorial Guinea, Rwanda, South Africa, Tanzania, and Uganda. There is no vaccine against Marburg. The United States CDC currently has a Level 1 – Practice Usual Precautions Travel Health Notice posted regarding Marburg in Ethiopia and has issued a Health Alert Network Health Advisory. Source: WHO (1/16/26) New World Screwworm Mexico – Animal Cases Reported in Tamaulipas Near United States Border: On January 20, 2026, the United States CDC issued a Health Advisory regarding New World screwworm (NWS) cases detected among animals near the United States – Mexico border, speciﬁcally in Tamaulipas, to increase awareness given the potential for geographic spread. According to data from the Secretary of Agriculture of Mexico, as of January 20, 2026, there have been a total of 14,321 NWS cases reported among animals, of which 870 are currently active, since November 2024. Activity in Mexico is primarily concentrated in central and southern areas. In Tamaulipas, there have been a total of 16 NWS cases reported, 13 of which are currently active. There have been over 1,190 NWS cases and 7 deaths reported among humans in Mexico (including 24 hospitalizations) and Central America, and 1 conﬁrmed NWS case reported in the United States among a traveler returning from El Salvador. According to the United States CDC, the NWS ﬂy has not been detected in the United States and the risk to humans is low. Central America has been experiencing a New World Screwworm outbreak since 2023. Figure Notes: Data as of January 20,2026. Because this report aggregates and summarizes data and information from outside sources, the quality, accuracy or completeness of that data, and the appropriateness of the methodology used, cannot be guaranteed. .......................................................................................................... 17 Chikungunya United States – Second Locally Acquired Case of 2025 Reported in Florida: According to data the Florida Department of Health (Florida Health), a locally acquired case of chikungunya was reported during the week ending January 17, 2026. The case was reported in Miami-Dade County and experienced symptom onset in December 2025. This is the only locally acquired case reported in Florida during 2025. Florida last reported local transmission of chikungunya in 2014. A total of 328 travel associated were reported during 2025, primarily among individuals with recent travel history to Cuba (316). In October 2025, the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH) reported the ﬁrst conﬁrmed locally acquired case of chikungunya ever in the state among an individual from Nassau County. According to data from the United States CDC, these are the ﬁrst locally acquired cases to be reported in the United States since 2015. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), a resurgence of chikungunya was observed in several regions globally during 2025, particularly in the Americas, with signiﬁcant potential for further spread and new introductions in previously unaﬀected areas. Source: Florida Health (1/26) 2 Diphtheria Nigeria – Resurgence Observed in 2022 Continues Through 2025: According to data from the Nigeria Center for Disease Control (NCDC), as of December 28, there have been a total of 20,032 suspected cases of diphtheria, of which 15,273 are conﬁrmed, and 872 deaths among conﬁrmed cases reported in Nigeria during 2025. Case and death totals for 2025 are higher and more geographically dispersed compared to 2024. The United States CDC currently has a Level 2 – Practice Enhanced Precautions Travel Health Notice posted regarding diphtheria in Nigeria. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), several countries in the African region reported a resurgence of diphtheria from 2023-2024, including Nigeria. Since 2022, Nigeria has reported a total of 61,570 suspected cases, of which 40,142 are conﬁrmed, and 2,143 deaths among conﬁrmed cases (CFR: 5.3%). Only 6.7% of conﬁrmed cases were fully vaccinated. No incident cases or deaths were reported since the previous update. There have been 5 recoveries and there are no contacts currently under follow up. A total of 40 days have passed without any incident cases reported – 42 days must pass for the outbreak to be declared over. Cases have been reported in Jinka town and Hawassa city, both locations in southern Ethiopia. Since the outbreak began, over 3,800 individuals have been tested for infection. This is the ﬁrst Marburg outbreak in Ethiopia – previous outbreaks and sporadic cases have been reported in other African counties, including Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Ghana, Kenya, Equatorial Guinea, Rwanda, South Africa, Tanzania, and Uganda. There is no vaccine against Marburg. The United States CDC currently has a Level 1 – Practice Usual Precautions Travel Health Notice posted regarding Marburg in Ethiopia and has issued a Health Alert Network Health Advisory. .......................................................................................................... 17 Chikungunya United States – Second Locally Acquired Case of 2025 Reported in Florida: According to data the Florida Department of Health (Florida Health), a locally acquired case of chikungunya was reported during the week ending January 17, 2026. The case was reported in Miami-Dade County and experienced symptom onset in December 2025. This is the only locally acquired case reported in Florida during 2025. Florida last reported local transmission of chikungunya in 2014. A total of 328 travel associated were reported during 2025, primarily among individuals with recent travel history to Cuba (316). In October 2025, the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH) reported the ﬁrst conﬁrmed locally acquired case of chikungunya ever in the state among an individual from Nassau County. According to data from the United States CDC, these are the ﬁrst locally acquired cases to be reported in the United States since 2015. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), a resurgence of chikungunya was observed in several regions globally during 2025, particularly in the Americas, with signiﬁcant potential for further spread and new introductions in previously unaﬀected areas. Source: Florida Health (1/26) 2 Diphtheria Nigeria – Resurgence Observed in 2022 Continues Through 2025: According to data from the Nigeria Center for Disease Control (NCDC), as of December 28, there have been a total of 20,032 suspected cases of diphtheria, of which 15,273 are conﬁrmed, and 872 deaths among conﬁrmed cases reported in Nigeria during 2025. Case and death totals for 2025 are higher and more geographically dispersed compared to 2024. No incident cases or deaths were reported since the previous update. There have been 5 recoveries and there are no contacts currently under follow up. A total of 40 days have passed without any incident cases reported – 42 days must pass for the outbreak to be declared over. Cases have been reported in Jinka town and Hawassa city, both locations in southern Ethiopia. Since the outbreak began, over 3,800 individuals have been tested for infection. This is the ﬁrst Marburg outbreak in Ethiopia – previous outbreaks and sporadic cases have been reported in other African counties, including Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Ghana, Kenya, Equatorial Guinea, Rwanda, South Africa, Tanzania, and Uganda. There is no vaccine against Marburg. .......................................................................................................... 17 Chikungunya United States – Second Locally Acquired Case of 2025 Reported in Florida: According to data the Florida Department of Health (Florida Health), a locally acquired case of chikungunya was reported during the week ending January 17, 2026. The case was reported in Miami-Dade County and experienced symptom onset in December 2025. This is the only locally acquired case reported in Florida during 2025. Florida last reported local transmission of chikungunya in 2014. A total of 328 travel associated were reported during 2025, primarily among individuals with recent travel history to Cuba (316). In October 2025, the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH) reported the ﬁrst conﬁrmed locally acquired case of chikungunya ever in the state among an individual from Nassau County. According to data from the United States CDC, these are the ﬁrst locally acquired cases to be reported in the United States since 2015. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), a resurgence of chikungunya was observed in several regions globally during 2025, particularly in the Americas, with signiﬁcant potential for further spread and new introductions in previously unaﬀected areas. Source: Florida Health (1/26) 2 Diphtheria Nigeria – Resurgence Observed in 2022 Continues Through 2025: According to data from the Nigeria Center for Disease Control (NCDC), as of December 28, there have been a total of 20,032 suspected cases of diphtheria, of which 15,273 are conﬁrmed, and 872 deaths among conﬁrmed cases reported in Nigeria during 2025. Case and death totals for 2025 are higher and more geographically dispersed compared to 2024. No incident cases or deaths were reported since the previous update. There have been 5 recoveries and there are no contacts currently under follow up. A total of 40 days have passed without any incident cases reported – 42 days must pass for the outbreak to be declared over. Cases have been reported in Jinka town and Hawassa city, both locations in southern Ethiopia. Since the outbreak began, over 3,800 individuals have been tested for infection. This is the ﬁrst Marburg outbreak in Ethiopia – previous outbreaks and sporadic cases have been reported in other African counties, including Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Ghana, Kenya, Equatorial Guinea, Rwanda, South Africa, Tanzania, and Uganda. There is no vaccine against Marburg. The Global Health Update summaries include preliminary and up-to-date data that are publicly available for these events at the time of posting. Because this report aggregates and summarizes data and information from outside sources, the quality, accuracy or completeness of that data, and the appropriateness of the methodology used, cannot be guaranteed. Please refer directly to those sources for any data questions. Because the report includes preliminary information, subsequent reports may contain updates or revisions to information in prior reports. .......................................................................................................... 17 Chikungunya United States – Second Locally Acquired Case of 2025 Reported in Florida: According to data the Florida Department of Health (Florida Health), a locally acquired case of chikungunya was reported during the week ending January 17, 2026. The case was reported in Miami-Dade County and experienced symptom onset in December 2025. This is the only locally acquired case reported in Florida during 2025. Florida last reported local transmission of chikungunya in 2014. A total of 328 travel associated were reported during 2025, primarily among individuals with recent travel history to Cuba (316). In October 2025, the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH) reported the ﬁrst conﬁrmed locally acquired case of chikungunya ever in the state among an individual from Nassau County. According to data from the United States CDC, these are the ﬁrst locally acquired cases to be reported in the United States since 2015. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), a resurgence of chikungunya was observed in several regions globally during 2025, particularly in the Americas, with signiﬁcant potential for further spread and new introductions in previously unaﬀected areas. Source: Florida Health (1/26) 2 Diphtheria Nigeria – Resurgence Observed in 2022 Continues Through 2025: According to data from the Nigeria Center for Disease Control (NCDC), as of December 28, there have been a total of 20,032 suspected cases of diphtheria, of which 15,273 are conﬁrmed, and 872 deaths among conﬁrmed cases reported in Nigeria during 2025. Case and death totals for 2025 are higher and more geographically dispersed compared to 2024. The United States CDC currently has a Level 2 – Practice Enhanced Precautions Travel Health Notice posted regarding diphtheria in Nigeria. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), several countries in the African region reported a resurgence of diphtheria from 2023-2024, including Nigeria. Since 2022, Nigeria has reported a total of 61,570 suspected cases, of which 40,142 are conﬁrmed, and 2,143 deaths among conﬁrmed cases (CFR: 5.3%). Only 6.7% of conﬁrmed cases were fully vaccinated. Most aﬀected states include Kano, Yobe, Katsina, Borno, and Bauchi. Demographically, females (61.1%) and those aged 1-14 (65.3%) have been aﬀected most. Source: NCDC Marburg Ethiopia – No Incident Cases Reported for 40 Consecutive Days: According to the Africa CDC, as of January 22, 2026, there have been 14 conﬁrmed Marburg cases and 9 deaths reported in Ethiopia since the outbreak was ﬁrst declared on November 14, 2025. No incident cases or deaths were reported since the previous update. There have been 5 recoveries and there are no contacts currently under follow up. A total of 40 days have passed without any incident cases reported – 42 days must pass for the outbreak to be declared over. Cases have been reported in Jinka town and Hawassa city, both locations in southern Ethiopia. Since the outbreak began, over 3,800 individuals have been tested for infection. This is the ﬁrst Marburg outbreak in Ethiopia – previous outbreaks and sporadic cases have been reported in other African counties, including Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Ghana, Kenya, Equatorial Guinea, Rwanda, South Africa, Tanzania, and Uganda. There is no vaccine against Marburg. The United States CDC currently has a Level 1 – Practice Usual Precautions Travel Health Notice posted regarding Marburg in Ethiopia and has issued a Health Alert Network Health Advisory. .......................................................................................................... 17 Chikungunya United States – Second Locally Acquired Case of 2025 Reported in Florida: According to data the Florida Department of Health (Florida Health), a locally acquired case of chikungunya was reported during the week ending January 17, 2026. The case was reported in Miami-Dade County and experienced symptom onset in December 2025. This is the only locally acquired case reported in Florida during 2025. Florida last reported local transmission of chikungunya in 2014. A total of 328 travel associated were reported during 2025, primarily among individuals with recent travel history to Cuba (316). In October 2025, the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH) reported the ﬁrst conﬁrmed locally acquired case of chikungunya ever in the state among an individual from Nassau County. According to data from the United States CDC, these are the ﬁrst locally acquired cases to be reported in the United States since 2015. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), a resurgence of chikungunya was observed in several regions globally during 2025, particularly in the Americas, with signiﬁcant potential for further spread and new introductions in previously unaﬀected areas. Source: Florida Health (1/26) 2 Diphtheria Nigeria – Resurgence Observed in 2022 Continues Through 2025: According to data from the Nigeria Center for Disease Control (NCDC), as of December 28, there have been a total of 20,032 suspected cases of diphtheria, of which 15,273 are conﬁrmed, and 872 deaths among conﬁrmed cases reported in Nigeria during 2025. Case and death totals for 2025 are higher and more geographically dispersed compared to 2024. The United States CDC currently has a Level 2 – Practice Enhanced Precautions Travel Health Notice posted regarding diphtheria in Nigeria. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), several countries in the African region reported a resurgence of diphtheria from 2023-2024, including Nigeria. Since 2022, Nigeria has reported a total of 61,570 suspected cases, of which 40,142 are conﬁrmed, and 2,143 deaths among conﬁrmed cases (CFR: 5.3%). Only 6.7% of conﬁrmed cases were fully vaccinated. Most aﬀected states include Kano, Yobe, Katsina, Borno, and Bauchi. Demographically, females (61.1%) and those aged 1-14 (65.3%) have been aﬀected most. No incident cases or deaths were reported since the previous update. There have been 5 recoveries and there are no contacts currently under follow up. A total of 40 days have passed without any incident cases reported – 42 days must pass for the outbreak to be declared over. Cases have been reported in Jinka town and Hawassa city, both locations in southern Ethiopia. Since the outbreak began, over 3,800 individuals have been tested for infection. This is the ﬁrst Marburg outbreak in Ethiopia – previous outbreaks and sporadic cases have been reported in other African counties, including Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Ghana, Kenya, Equatorial Guinea, Rwanda, South Africa, Tanzania, and Uganda. There is no vaccine against Marburg. The United States CDC currently has a Level 1 – Practice Usual Precautions Travel Health Notice posted regarding Marburg in Ethiopia and has issued a Health Alert Network Health Advisory. .......................................................................................................... 17 Chikungunya United States – Second Locally Acquired Case of 2025 Reported in Florida: According to data the Florida Department of Health (Florida Health), a locally acquired case of chikungunya was reported during the week ending January 17, 2026. The case was reported in Miami-Dade County and experienced symptom onset in December 2025. This is the only locally acquired case reported in Florida during 2025. Florida last reported local transmission of chikungunya in 2014. A total of 328 travel associated were reported during 2025, primarily among individuals with recent travel history to Cuba (316). In October 2025, the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH) reported the ﬁrst conﬁrmed locally acquired case of chikungunya ever in the state among an individual from Nassau County. According to data from the United States CDC, these are the ﬁrst locally acquired cases to be reported in the United States since 2015. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), a resurgence of chikungunya was observed in several regions globally during 2025, particularly in the Americas, with signiﬁcant potential for further spread and new introductions in previously unaﬀected areas. Source: Florida Health (1/26) 2 Diphtheria Nigeria – Resurgence Observed in 2022 Continues Through 2025: According to data from the Nigeria Center for Disease Control (NCDC), as of December 28, there have been a total of 20,032 suspected cases of diphtheria, of which 15,273 are conﬁrmed, and 872 deaths among conﬁrmed cases reported in Nigeria during 2025. Case and death totals for 2025 are higher and more geographically dispersed compared to 2024. No incident cases or deaths were reported since the previous update. There have been 5 recoveries and there are no contacts currently under follow up. A total of 40 days have passed without any incident cases reported – 42 days must pass for the outbreak to be declared over. Cases have been reported in Jinka town and Hawassa city, both locations in southern Ethiopia. Since the outbreak began, over 3,800 individuals have been tested for infection. This is the ﬁrst Marburg outbreak in Ethiopia – previous outbreaks and sporadic cases have been reported in other African counties, including Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Ghana, Kenya, Equatorial Guinea, Rwanda, South Africa, Tanzania, and Uganda. There is no vaccine against Marburg. The United States CDC currently has a Level 1 – Practice Usual Precautions Travel Health Notice posted regarding Marburg in Ethiopia and has issued a Health Alert Network Health Advisory. .......................................................................................................... 17 Chikungunya United States – Second Locally Acquired Case of 2025 Reported in Florida: According to data the Florida Department of Health (Florida Health), a locally acquired case of chikungunya was reported during the week ending January 17, 2026. The case was reported in Miami-Dade County and experienced symptom onset in December 2025. This is the only locally acquired case reported in Florida during 2025. Florida last reported local transmission of chikungunya in 2014. A total of 328 travel associated were reported during 2025, primarily among individuals with recent travel history to Cuba (316). In October 2025, the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH) reported the ﬁrst conﬁrmed locally acquired case of chikungunya ever in the state among an individual from Nassau County. According to data from the United States CDC, these are the ﬁrst locally acquired cases to be reported in the United States since 2015. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), a resurgence of chikungunya was observed in several regions globally during 2025, particularly in the Americas, with signiﬁcant potential for further spread and new introductions in previously unaﬀected areas. Source: Florida Health (1/26) 2 Diphtheria Nigeria – Resurgence Observed in 2022 Continues Through 2025: According to data from the Nigeria Center for Disease Control (NCDC), as of December 28, there have been a total of 20,032 suspected cases of diphtheria, of which 15,273 are conﬁrmed, and 872 deaths among conﬁrmed cases reported in Nigeria during 2025. Case and death totals for 2025 are higher and more geographically dispersed compared to 2024. The United States CDC currently has a Level 2 – Practice Enhanced Precautions Travel Health Notice posted regarding diphtheria in Nigeria. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), several countries in the African region reported a resurgence of diphtheria from 2023-2024, including Nigeria. Since 2022, Nigeria has reported a total of 61,570 suspected cases, of which 40,142 are conﬁrmed, and 2,143 deaths among conﬁrmed cases (CFR: 5.3%). Only 6.7% of conﬁrmed cases were fully vaccinated. No incident cases or deaths were reported since the previous update. There have been 5 recoveries and there are no contacts currently under follow up. A total of 40 days have passed without any incident cases reported – 42 days must pass for the outbreak to be declared over. Cases have been reported in Jinka town and Hawassa city, both locations in southern Ethiopia. Since the outbreak began, over 3,800 individuals have been tested for infection. This is the ﬁrst Marburg outbreak in Ethiopia – previous outbreaks and sporadic cases have been reported in other African counties, including Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Ghana, Kenya, Equatorial Guinea, Rwanda, South Africa, Tanzania, and Uganda. There is no vaccine against Marburg. The United States CDC currently has a Level 1 – Practice Usual Precautions Travel Health Notice posted regarding Marburg in Ethiopia and has issued a Health Alert Network Health Advisory. .......................................................................................................... 17 Chikungunya United States – Second Locally Acquired Case of 2025 Reported in Florida: According to data the Florida Department of Health (Florida Health), a locally acquired case of chikungunya was reported during the week ending January 17, 2026. The case was reported in Miami-Dade County and experienced symptom onset in December 2025. This is the only locally acquired case reported in Florida during 2025. Florida last reported local transmission of chikungunya in 2014. A total of 328 travel associated were reported during 2025, primarily among individuals with recent travel history to Cuba (316). In October 2025, the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH) reported the ﬁrst conﬁrmed locally acquired case of chikungunya ever in the state among an individual from Nassau County. According to data from the United States CDC, these are the ﬁrst locally acquired cases to be reported in the United States since 2015. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), a resurgence of chikungunya was observed in several regions globally during 2025, particularly in the Americas, with signiﬁcant potential for further spread and new introductions in previously unaﬀected areas. Source: Florida Health (1/26) 2 Diphtheria Nigeria – Resurgence Observed in 2022 Continues Through 2025: According to data from the Nigeria Center for Disease Control (NCDC), as of December 28, there have been a total of 20,032 suspected cases of diphtheria, of which 15,273 are conﬁrmed, and 872 deaths among conﬁrmed cases reported in Nigeria during 2025. Case and death totals for 2025 are higher and more geographically dispersed compared to 2024. The United States CDC currently has a Level 2 – Practice Enhanced Precautions Travel Health Notice posted regarding diphtheria in Nigeria. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), several countries in the African region reported a resurgence of diphtheria from 2023-2024, including Nigeria. Since 2022, Nigeria has reported a total of 61,570 suspected cases, of which 40,142 are conﬁrmed, and 2,143 deaths among conﬁrmed cases (CFR: 5.3%). Only 6.7% of conﬁrmed cases were fully vaccinated. Most aﬀected states include Kano, Yobe, Katsina, Borno, and Bauchi. Demographically, females (61.1%) and those aged 1-14 (65.3%) have been aﬀected most. No incident cases or deaths were reported since the previous update. There have been 5 recoveries and there are no contacts currently under follow up. A total of 40 days have passed without any incident cases reported – 42 days must pass for the outbreak to be declared over. Cases have been reported in Jinka town and Hawassa city, both locations in southern Ethiopia. Since the outbreak began, over 3,800 individuals have been tested for infection. This is the ﬁrst Marburg outbreak in Ethiopia – previous outbreaks and sporadic cases have been reported in other African counties, including Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Ghana, Kenya, Equatorial Guinea, Rwanda, South Africa, Tanzania, and Uganda. There is no vaccine against Marburg. The United States CDC currently has a Level 1 – Practice Usual Precautions Travel Health Notice posted regarding Marburg in Ethiopia and has issued a Health Alert Network Health Advisory. .......................................................................................................... 17 Chikungunya United States – Second Locally Acquired Case of 2025 Reported in Florida: According to data the Florida Department of Health (Florida Health), a locally acquired case of chikungunya was reported during the week ending January 17, 2026. The case was reported in Miami-Dade County and experienced symptom onset in December 2025. This is the only locally acquired case reported in Florida during 2025. Florida last reported local transmission of chikungunya in 2014. A total of 328 travel associated were reported during 2025, primarily among individuals with recent travel history to Cuba (316). In October 2025, the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH) reported the ﬁrst conﬁrmed locally acquired case of chikungunya ever in the state among an individual from Nassau County. According to data from the United States CDC, these are the ﬁrst locally acquired cases to be reported in the United States since 2015. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), a resurgence of chikungunya was observed in several regions globally during 2025, particularly in the Americas, with signiﬁcant potential for further spread and new introductions in previously unaﬀected areas. Source: Florida Health (1/26) 2 Diphtheria Nigeria – Resurgence Observed in 2022 Continues Through 2025: According to data from the Nigeria Center for Disease Control (NCDC), as of December 28, there have been a total of 20,032 suspected cases of diphtheria, of which 15,273 are conﬁrmed, and 872 deaths among conﬁrmed cases reported in Nigeria during 2025. Case and death totals for 2025 are higher and more geographically dispersed compared to 2024. No incident cases or deaths were reported since the previous update. There have been 5 recoveries and there are no contacts currently under follow up. A total of 40 days have passed without any incident cases reported – 42 days must pass for the outbreak to be declared over. .......................................................................................................... 17 Chikungunya United States – Second Locally Acquired Case of 2025 Reported in Florida: According to data the Florida Department of Health (Florida Health), a locally acquired case of chikungunya was reported during the week ending January 17, 2026. The case was reported in Miami-Dade County and experienced symptom onset in December 2025. This is the only locally acquired case reported in Florida during 2025. Florida last reported local transmission of chikungunya in 2014. A total of 328 travel associated were reported during 2025, primarily among individuals with recent travel history to Cuba (316). In October 2025, the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH) reported the ﬁrst conﬁrmed locally acquired case of chikungunya ever in the state among an individual from Nassau County. According to data from the United States CDC, these are the ﬁrst locally acquired cases to be reported in the United States since 2015. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), a resurgence of chikungunya was observed in several regions globally during 2025, particularly in the Americas, with signiﬁcant potential for further spread and new introductions in previously unaﬀected areas. Source: Florida Health (1/26) 2 Diphtheria Nigeria – Resurgence Observed in 2022 Continues Through 2025: According to data from the Nigeria Center for Disease Control (NCDC), as of December 28, there have been a total of 20,032 suspected cases of diphtheria, of which 15,273 are conﬁrmed, and 872 deaths among conﬁrmed cases reported in Nigeria during 2025. Case and death totals for 2025 are higher and more geographically dispersed compared to 2024. No incident cases or deaths were reported since the previous update. There have been 5 recoveries and there are no contacts currently under follow up. A total of 40 days have passed without any incident cases reported – 42 days must pass for the outbreak to be declared over. Cases have been reported in Jinka town and Hawassa city, both locations in southern Ethiopia. Since the outbreak began, over 3,800 individuals have been tested for infection. This is the ﬁrst Marburg outbreak in Ethiopia – previous outbreaks and sporadic cases have been reported in other African counties, including Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Ghana, Kenya, Equatorial Guinea, Rwanda, South Africa, Tanzania, and Uganda. There is no vaccine against Marburg. .......................................................................................................... 17 Chikungunya United States – Second Locally Acquired Case of 2025 Reported in Florida: According to data the Florida Department of Health (Florida Health), a locally acquired case of chikungunya was reported during the week ending January 17, 2026. The case was reported in Miami-Dade County and experienced symptom onset in December 2025. This is the only locally acquired case reported in Florida during 2025. Florida last reported local transmission of chikungunya in 2014. A total of 328 travel associated were reported during 2025, primarily among individuals with recent travel history to Cuba (316). In October 2025, the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH) reported the ﬁrst conﬁrmed locally acquired case of chikungunya ever in the state among an individual from Nassau County. According to data from the United States CDC, these are the ﬁrst locally acquired cases to be reported in the United States since 2015. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), a resurgence of chikungunya was observed in several regions globally during 2025, particularly in the Americas, with signiﬁcant potential for further spread and new introductions in previously unaﬀected areas. Source: Florida Health (1/26) 2 Diphtheria Nigeria – Resurgence Observed in 2022 Continues Through 2025: According to data from the Nigeria Center for Disease Control (NCDC), as of December 28, there have been a total of 20,032 suspected cases of diphtheria, of which 15,273 are conﬁrmed, and 872 deaths among conﬁrmed cases reported in Nigeria during 2025. Case and death totals for 2025 are higher and more geographically dispersed compared to 2024. The United States CDC currently has a Level 2 – Practice Enhanced Precautions Travel Health Notice posted regarding diphtheria in Nigeria. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), several countries in the African region reported a resurgence of diphtheria from 2023-2024, including Nigeria. Since 2022, Nigeria has reported a total of 61,570 suspected cases, of which 40,142 are conﬁrmed, and 2,143 deaths among conﬁrmed cases (CFR: 5.3%). Only 6.7% of conﬁrmed cases were fully vaccinated. Most aﬀected states include Kano, Yobe, Katsina, Borno, and Bauchi. Demographically, females (61.1%) and those aged 1-14 (65.3%) have been aﬀected most. The Global Health Update summaries include preliminary and up-to-date data that are publicly available for these events at the time of posting. Because this report aggregates and summarizes data and information from outside sources, the quality, accuracy or completeness of that data, and the appropriateness of the methodology used, cannot be guaranteed. Please refer directly to those sources for any data questions. .......................................................................................................... 17 Chikungunya United States – Second Locally Acquired Case of 2025 Reported in Florida: According to data the Florida Department of Health (Florida Health), a locally acquired case of chikungunya was reported during the week ending January 17, 2026. The case was reported in Miami-Dade County and experienced symptom onset in December 2025. This is the only locally acquired case reported in Florida during 2025. Florida last reported local transmission of chikungunya in 2014. A total of 328 travel associated were reported during 2025, primarily among individuals with recent travel history to Cuba (316). In October 2025, the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH) reported the ﬁrst conﬁrmed locally acquired case of chikungunya ever in the state among an individual from Nassau County. According to data from the United States CDC, these are the ﬁrst locally acquired cases to be reported in the United States since 2015. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), a resurgence of chikungunya was observed in several regions globally during 2025, particularly in the Americas, with signiﬁcant potential for further spread and new introductions in previously unaﬀected areas. Source: Florida Health (1/26) 2 Diphtheria Nigeria – Resurgence Observed in 2022 Continues Through 2025: According to data from the Nigeria Center for Disease Control (NCDC), as of December 28, there have been a total of 20,032 suspected cases of diphtheria, of which 15,273 are conﬁrmed, and 872 deaths among conﬁrmed cases reported in Nigeria during 2025. Case and death totals for 2025 are higher and more geographically dispersed compared to 2024. The United States CDC currently has a Level 2 – Practice Enhanced Precautions Travel Health Notice posted regarding diphtheria in Nigeria. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), several countries in the African region reported a resurgence of diphtheria from 2023-2024, including Nigeria. Since 2022, Nigeria has reported a total of 61,570 suspected cases, of which 40,142 are conﬁrmed, and 2,143 deaths among conﬁrmed cases (CFR: 5.3%). Only 6.7% of conﬁrmed cases were fully vaccinated. Most aﬀected states include Kano, Yobe, Katsina, Borno, and Bauchi. Demographically, females (61.1%) and those aged 1-14 (65.3%) have been aﬀected most. Source: NCDC Marburg Ethiopia – No Incident Cases Reported for 40 Consecutive Days: According to the Africa CDC, as of January 22, 2026, there have been 14 conﬁrmed Marburg cases and 9 deaths reported in Ethiopia since the outbreak was ﬁrst declared on November 14, 2025. No incident cases or deaths were reported since the previous update. There have been 5 recoveries and there are no contacts currently under follow up. A total of 40 days have passed without any incident cases reported – 42 days must pass for the outbreak to be declared over. Cases have been reported in Jinka town and Hawassa city, both locations in southern Ethiopia. Since the outbreak began, over 3,800 individuals have been tested for infection. This is the ﬁrst Marburg outbreak in Ethiopia – previous outbreaks and sporadic cases have been reported in other African counties, including Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Ghana, Kenya, Equatorial Guinea, Rwanda, South Africa, Tanzania, and Uganda. There is no vaccine against Marburg. The United States CDC currently has a Level 1 – Practice Usual Precautions Travel Health Notice posted regarding Marburg in Ethiopia and has issued a Health Alert Network Health Advisory. Source: Africa CDC (1/22/26), CDC (12/22/25) Measles Canada – Initial Data for 2026; Incident Cases Reported in Multiple Provinces: According to data from the Public Health Agency of Canada (PHAC), as of January 10, there have been a total of 17 probable and conﬁrmed measles cases reported in Canada during 2026. .......................................................................................................... 17 Chikungunya United States – Second Locally Acquired Case of 2025 Reported in Florida: According to data the Florida Department of Health (Florida Health), a locally acquired case of chikungunya was reported during the week ending January 17, 2026. The case was reported in Miami-Dade County and experienced symptom onset in December 2025. This is the only locally acquired case reported in Florida during 2025. Florida last reported local transmission of chikungunya in 2014. A total of 328 travel associated were reported during 2025, primarily among individuals with recent travel history to Cuba (316). In October 2025, the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH) reported the ﬁrst conﬁrmed locally acquired case of chikungunya ever in the state among an individual from Nassau County. According to data from the United States CDC, these are the ﬁrst locally acquired cases to be reported in the United States since 2015. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), a resurgence of chikungunya was observed in several regions globally during 2025, particularly in the Americas, with signiﬁcant potential for further spread and new introductions in previously unaﬀected areas. Source: Florida Health (1/26) 2 Diphtheria Nigeria – Resurgence Observed in 2022 Continues Through 2025: According to data from the Nigeria Center for Disease Control (NCDC), as of December 28, there have been a total of 20,032 suspected cases of diphtheria, of which 15,273 are conﬁrmed, and 872 deaths among conﬁrmed cases reported in Nigeria during 2025. Case and death totals for 2025 are higher and more geographically dispersed compared to 2024. No incident cases or deaths were reported since the previous update. There have been 5 recoveries and there are no contacts currently under follow up. A total of 40 days have passed without any incident cases reported – 42 days must pass for the outbreak to be declared over. Cases have been reported in Jinka town and Hawassa city, both locations in southern Ethiopia. Since the outbreak began, over 3,800 individuals have been tested for infection. This is the ﬁrst Marburg outbreak in Ethiopia – previous outbreaks and sporadic cases have been reported in other African counties, including Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Ghana, Kenya, Equatorial Guinea, Rwanda, South Africa, Tanzania, and Uganda. There is no vaccine against Marburg. .......................................................................................................... 17 Chikungunya United States – Second Locally Acquired Case of 2025 Reported in Florida: According to data the Florida Department of Health (Florida Health), a locally acquired case of chikungunya was reported during the week ending January 17, 2026. The case was reported in Miami-Dade County and experienced symptom onset in December 2025. This is the only locally acquired case reported in Florida during 2025. Florida last reported local transmission of chikungunya in 2014. A total of 328 travel associated were reported during 2025, primarily among individuals with recent travel history to Cuba (316). In October 2025, the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH) reported the ﬁrst conﬁrmed locally acquired case of chikungunya ever in the state among an individual from Nassau County. According to data from the United States CDC, these are the ﬁrst locally acquired cases to be reported in the United States since 2015. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), a resurgence of chikungunya was observed in several regions globally during 2025, particularly in the Americas, with signiﬁcant potential for further spread and new introductions in previously unaﬀected areas. Source: Florida Health (1/26) 2 Diphtheria Nigeria – Resurgence Observed in 2022 Continues Through 2025: According to data from the Nigeria Center for Disease Control (NCDC), as of December 28, there have been a total of 20,032 suspected cases of diphtheria, of which 15,273 are conﬁrmed, and 872 deaths among conﬁrmed cases reported in Nigeria during 2025. Case and death totals for 2025 are higher and more geographically dispersed compared to 2024. No incident cases or deaths were reported since the previous update. There have been 5 recoveries and there are no contacts currently under follow up. A total of 40 days have passed without any incident cases reported – 42 days must pass for the outbreak to be declared over. Cases have been reported in Jinka town and Hawassa city, both locations in southern Ethiopia. Since the outbreak began, over 3,800 individuals have been tested for infection. This is the ﬁrst Marburg outbreak in Ethiopia – previous outbreaks and sporadic cases have been reported in other African counties, including Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Ghana, Kenya, Equatorial Guinea, Rwanda, South Africa, Tanzania, and Uganda. There is no vaccine against Marburg. .......................................................................................................... 17 Chikungunya United States – Second Locally Acquired Case of 2025 Reported in Florida: According to data the Florida Department of Health (Florida Health), a locally acquired case of chikungunya was reported during the week ending January 17, 2026. The case was reported in Miami-Dade County and experienced symptom onset in December 2025. This is the only locally acquired case reported in Florida during 2025. Florida last reported local transmission of chikungunya in 2014. A total of 328 travel associated were reported during 2025, primarily among individuals with recent travel history to Cuba (316). In October 2025, the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH) reported the ﬁrst conﬁrmed locally acquired case of chikungunya ever in the state among an individual from Nassau County. According to data from the United States CDC, these are the ﬁrst locally acquired cases to be reported in the United States since 2015. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), a resurgence of chikungunya was observed in several regions globally during 2025, particularly in the Americas, with signiﬁcant potential for further spread and new introductions in previously unaﬀected areas. Source: Florida Health (1/26) 2 Diphtheria Nigeria – Resurgence Observed in 2022 Continues Through 2025: According to data from the Nigeria Center for Disease Control (NCDC), as of December 28, there have been a total of 20,032 suspected cases of diphtheria, of which 15,273 are conﬁrmed, and 872 deaths among conﬁrmed cases reported in Nigeria during 2025. Case and death totals for 2025 are higher and more geographically dispersed compared to 2024.
